summary: Pursued the last sourced lead on the decision-formation axis and reproduced it: a restarted node that forgets a voter whose addition is committed in its own log holds a smaller quorum than the committed configuration. In the four-voter probe (bootstrap {A,B,C}, AddVoter D committed, then restart the leader with RestoreCommittedLogs) the restarted leader reports three servers while the other nodes report four, and after partitioning C and D from A a single Apply succeeds — A commits and applies the entry at index 8 while C sits at 7 and D at 6, so only two of the four committed voters hold it; the control without the flag refuses the same write ('leadership lost while committing log'). This is a distinct direction from the resurrected-voter case (understated rather than resurrected membership) and it is registered as a second child of the same question with four comparisons; the harness is self-contained, verified in an isolated copy of the captured tree, and fresh execution is requested. The parent interpretation notes the pending receipt.
